newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 1st half consolidated public surplus up.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 1st half consolidated public surplus up.

text.p: The Philippines' consolidated public sector surplus in the first half of this year more than tripled to 14.13 billion pesos compared with 4.14 billion pesos in the year-ago period, the Department of Finance reported on Wednesday.
The government said the higher surplus in the consolidated public sector was largely due to the 9.74 billion pesos surplus of the national government.

Net cash inflows from two state pension funds amounting to 8.3 billion pesos, Central Bank's net income of 5.5 billion pesos and the positive cash flow in the state-run buffer fund of 5.2 billion pesos also enhanced the financial position of the consolidated public sector.

Finance Secretary Roberto De Ocampo said the surplus will help dampen inflation which has slowed to 7.9 percent in August from a year-high of 11.8 percent in March. The bellwhether 91-day Treasury bill rate had also declined to 11.3 percent from a peak of 13.2 percent in May.
The consolidated public sector surplus is expected to be balanced out by year-end with the acceleration of infrastructure spending, De Ocampo said.
